rules: Every Grace script picks its spoken hook options from here first (plus the coach-modeled hooks, PLAYBOOK §3); name the hook id in the plan's line sources. Ids match the sheet row: H016 = row 16.
Say hooks WORD FOR WORD as written in the sheet, no contractions or rewording (Ralph, 2026-10-05). Only the blanks (__) get filled; the humanizer pass leaves the hook line itself alone.
Fill every blank with a concrete moment from the product research, never a broad problem.
The line after the hook answers or proves it on screen right away (demo, close-up, the back/side/pocket shot).
Spread hook types across a product's videos (no two videos of one product on the same id; TikTok flags repeats).
Hooks marked 'Grace caution' clash with a house rule (only our product, no price): follow the caution.
These are spoken hooks. On-screen text stays curiosity-only, 5-7 words, and is burned in only on Ralph's yes.
Log which id each finished video used (`used_in`) so results can show which hook types win.
Types are as in the sheet; 'Comparison Hook', 'Time Pressure Hook' and 'Simple Fix Hook' are filed as Comparison, Time Pressure and Simple Fix.

hooks.hook: This is the part I actually care about
hooks.use_when: You want to lead with a specific detail, feature, or payoff that matters more than the obvious selling point.
hooks.note: Helps the creator center the video around one meaningful detail instead of trying to explain everything.

hooks.hook: I keep reaching for this more than I expected
hooks.use_when: You're showing a product that has quietly become part of your normal day, outfit, setup, or routine.
hooks.note: Feels natural and experience-based without needing a dramatic transformation or problem.

hooks.hook: This just makes everything feel a little more put together
hooks.use_when: You're selling the feeling the product creates rather than a major functional result.
hooks.note: Gives creators a softer way to talk about aesthetic or emotional payoff without overhyping the product.

hooks.hook: One thing I cannot stand is __
hooks.use_when: The product solves a very specific annoyance people immediately recognize.
hooks.note: Be specific about the annoying moment. The blank should not be a broad problem.

hooks.hook: I did not realize how much __ bothered me until I stopped dealing with it
hooks.use_when: The benefit is easier to appreciate after experiencing the alternative.
hooks.note: Works best when you can visibly show what changed.

hooks.hook: I have been putting up with this for way too long
hooks.use_when: The buyer may have normalized an irritating problem.
hooks.note: Name the actual thing you were putting up with quickly.

hooks.hook: If you also hate when __, look at this
hooks.use_when: The product solves minor everyday friction.
hooks.note: Fill the blank with a concrete situation, not a vague pain point.

hooks.hook: This is such a small thing, but it annoys me every single time
hooks.use_when: You're talking about a small, recurring annoyance that isn't dramatic, but happens often enough to make the product feel useful.
hooks.note: Small frustrations can be more believable than dramatic ones.

hooks.hook: Why did nobody make this easier sooner?
hooks.use_when: The solution feels obvious once viewers see it.
hooks.note: Let the demonstration answer the question.

hooks.hook: I am done pretending this does not bother me
hooks.use_when: The problem is relatable but people rarely say it out loud.
hooks.note: Keep the tone playful rather than dramatic.

hooks.hook: I know this is minor, but I really do care about __
hooks.use_when: A specific preference drives the purchase.
hooks.note: The specificity is the hook.

hooks.hook: Apparently I have very strong opinions about __
hooks.use_when: The product connects to a personal standard.
hooks.note: Follow immediately with the preference.

hooks.hook: I am very particular about __
hooks.use_when: The viewer may share a strong product preference.
hooks.note: Explain what your standard actually is.

hooks.hook: I do not need __ to be fancy. I just need it to __
hooks.use_when: The buyer values function over bells and whistles.
hooks.note: The second blank should be the real payoff.

hooks.hook: I like __, but I do not like __
hooks.use_when: The product gives the desired benefit without a common downside.
hooks.note: One of the strongest structures for showing a tradeoff.

hooks.hook: I want __ without having to __
hooks.use_when: The product removes an unwanted tradeoff.
hooks.note: Make both sides specific and believable.

hooks.hook: I am willing to deal with a lot, but not __
hooks.use_when: A small frustration has become the breaking point.
hooks.note: Best when the annoyance is visually obvious.

hooks.hook: I would rather __ than spend another day __
hooks.use_when: The product lets the buyer avoid something frustrating.
hooks.note: Keep the comparison natural, not exaggerated.

hooks.hook: This is the part I wanted to see before I bought it
hooks.use_when: The listing or other videos do not clearly answer an important purchase question.
hooks.note: Show the answer immediately after the hook.

hooks.hook: Okay, but what does the back actually look like?
hooks.use_when: The back view matters to the buying decision.
hooks.note: Excellent for products where creators usually only show the front.

hooks.hook: Does it actually have usable pockets?
hooks.use_when: Pocket size or placement matters.
hooks.note: Put your hands or real items inside them.

hooks.hook: I needed to know how this looked from the side
hooks.use_when: The side profile may reveal fit, shape, bulk, or coverage.
hooks.note: Show rather than over-explain.

hooks.hook: The first thing I checked was __
hooks.use_when: There is one feature buyers are likely to inspect first.
hooks.note: Name a real buying concern.

hooks.hook: Here is what I would want someone to show me before I ordered this
hooks.use_when: The product has several details that matter more than the listing.
hooks.note: Pick one or two details for this video, not every feature.

hooks.hook: I kept looking for a video that showed __
hooks.use_when: Existing content leaves an important question unanswered.
hooks.note: Great opportunity for search-friendly content.

hooks.hook: Before you buy this, look at __
hooks.use_when: The buyer needs to inspect one important detail.
hooks.note: Avoid fear-based wording. Make it useful.

hooks.hook: If you are wondering whether __, here you go
hooks.use_when: You can directly answer a likely buyer question.
hooks.note: Demonstrate the answer instead of talking around it.

hooks.hook: The listing did not really show me this part
hooks.use_when: A visual detail is clearer in real life than online
hooks.note: Close-up footage makes this stronger.

hooks.hook: This looks completely different once you actually see it on
hooks.use_when: The on-body or in-use appearance is the selling point
hooks.note: Show the product quickly.

hooks.hook: I did not realize how __ this was until I had it in my hand
hooks.use_when: Scale, weight, texture, thickness, or construction surprises you
hooks.note: Use your hand for visual scale when helpful.

hooks.hook: This is one of those details you do not notice until you use it
hooks.use_when: A feature becomes meaningful only during actual use
hooks.note: Show the use moment.

hooks.hook: I thought __ would be the best part, but it is actually __
hooks.use_when: A secondary feature becomes the real reason you like it
hooks.note: The contrast creates natural curiosity.

hooks.hook: The thing that sold me was not even the obvious feature
hooks.use_when: An overlooked detail is more compelling than the headline feature
hooks.note: Reveal the unexpected detail quickly.

hooks.hook: I was not expecting to care this much about __
hooks.use_when: A small feature turns out to matter more than expected
hooks.note: Works well with everyday conveniences.

hooks.hook: This is probably my favorite part and I almost missed it
hooks.use_when: A less-visible feature deserves attention
hooks.note: Show the feature as you name it.

hooks.hook: I bought it because of __, but I keep using it because of __
hooks.use_when: The initial reason to buy differs from the long-term payoff
hooks.note: Strong for products you have used more than once.

hooks.hook: I thought I would use this for __, but somehow it became my __
hooks.use_when: The product found an unexpected role in your life
hooks.note: Keep the second use believable and specific.

hooks.hook: I did not buy this for __, but that is exactly what I keep using it for
hooks.use_when: A secondary use case is surprisingly useful
hooks.note: A good way to create another video from an established product.

hooks.hook: This was supposed to be for __
hooks.use_when: Someone else in the household claimed or adopted the product
hooks.note: Let the little story carry the hook.

hooks.hook: I bought one and apparently that was my first mistake
hooks.use_when: Multiple family members or uses make one product insufficient

hooks.hook: This has somehow become the thing everyone in my house uses
hooks.use_when: Shared household usefulness is a selling point
hooks.note: Show different use moments if possible.

hooks.hook: I did not think this would become part of my routine
hooks.use_when: The product naturally earned a repeat-use spot

hooks.hook: This is one of those things I keep reaching for without thinking about it
hooks.use_when: The product has become naturally habitual
hooks.note: Show where you keep it or when you grab it.

hooks.hook: I keep this right by __ because that is where I actually use it
hooks.use_when: Placement explains how the product fits real life

hooks.hook: This stays in my __ for a reason
hooks.use_when: The product earns a permanent place somewhere

hooks.hook: This is the thing I grab when __
hooks.use_when: A recurring situation triggers use

hooks.hook: Every time I __, I end up reaching for this
hooks.use_when: The product fits a repeatable behavior

hooks.hook: I did not realize I had a routine for this until I noticed I always grab this first

hooks.hook: There is one time of day when I always want this
hooks.use_when: The product has a strong time-based use case

hooks.hook: This makes more sense once you see when I actually use it

hooks.hook: I save this specifically for __
hooks.use_when: The product has a distinct moment or event when it shines

hooks.hook: This is what I reach for when I want __
hooks.use_when: The product supports a specific desired feeling or result

hooks.hook: This is my __ kind of product
hooks.use_when: The product fits a recognizable personal preference or lifestyle

hooks.hook: I already know exactly who would love this
hooks.use_when: The product clearly fits a type of person

hooks.hook: This immediately made me think of my __
hooks.use_when: The product connects to a relationship or person

hooks.hook: This feels very __
hooks.use_when: The product has a clear aesthetic or personality

hooks.hook: If you are a __ person, you will understand why I noticed this
hooks.use_when: A niche preference makes the feature especially relevant
hooks.note: The identity should be specific enough to create recognition.

hooks.hook: I know exactly the kind of person who is going to care about this detail
hooks.use_when: A specific feature matters strongly to a particular buyer

hooks.hook: I am absolutely the person who __

hooks.hook: This is for the people who always __

hooks.hook: Please tell me I am not the only person who does this

hooks.hook: This is such a specific problem, but if you have it, you know

hooks.hook: You either care about this detail or you really do not

hooks.hook: This might sound picky, but __

hooks.hook: Maybe it is just me, but I always notice __

hooks.hook: I never know how to explain why I like __ until I see something like this

hooks.hook: I did not think there was a difference until I put them next to each other

hooks.hook: This is one of those things you have to see side by side

hooks.grace_caution: Needs two items on screen. Grace shows only our product: use it for two of our own variants/sizes, or our product vs. an unbranded 'what I used before'.

hooks.hook: Same idea. Completely different experience.

hooks.note: Immediately explain what creates the difference.
hooks.grace_caution: Needs two items on screen. Grace shows only our product: use it for two of our own variants/sizes, or our product vs. an unbranded 'what I used before'.

hooks.hook: I thought these would feel basically the same

hooks.grace_caution: Needs two items on screen. Grace shows only our product: use it for two of our own variants/sizes, or our product vs. an unbranded 'what I used before'.

hooks.hook: This is why I picked this version instead

hooks.grace_caution: Needs two items on screen. Grace shows only our product: use it for two of our own variants/sizes, or our product vs. an unbranded 'what I used before'.

hooks.hook: I did not need more __, I needed a better __

hooks.hook: Maybe the problem is not __

hooks.hook: I finally admitted that I just do not like __

hooks.hook: I thought I needed __, but what I really cared about was __

hooks.hook: I do not need this to do everything

hooks.hook: This does one thing I really wanted it to do

hooks.hook: This is the part that makes it worth it for me
